title: Module 7 quiz — JVM Internals and Performance
description: Eight questions on HotSpot memory, class loading, JIT, GC, allocation, and containers for BayPay’s Java 21 payment-service. Synthetic only.

questions.prompt: jcmd GC.heap_info on payment-service shows a 2g heap that is 40% used. RSS is 3.1g. What is the honest reading?
choices: The process is leaking 1.1g of Java objects
Heap used is not RSS; stacks, metaspace, native, and GC overhead also live in the process
You must set -Xmx equal to RSS
G1 is broken because RSS exceeds -Xmx
questions.explanation: Heap is one region. RSS includes thread stacks, metaspace, code cache, native libraries, and allocator waste. NMT is how you name the rest.

questions.prompt: Avery Chen’s payment request allocates a Money record and a Payment entity. Which statement is true?
choices: Both always die in TLAB and never become heap objects
Money is a value object in the domain; the JVM may still allocate unless escape analysis proves otherwise
questions.explanation: Domain immutability is not scalar replacement. Measure allocation. Escape analysis is a maybe, not a contract.

questions.prompt: Why is -Xcomp a bad default on pay-prod-east-2?
choices: It forces compilation of cold code, increases startup and code-cache pressure, and is not a substitute for a production profiler
It is required for Spring Boot 3.5
questions.explanation: C1/C2 need warmup and profiling. -Xcomp compiles everything early. Use it as a diagnostic curiosity, not a prod flag.

questions.prompt: A GC log shows frequent young collections and rare mixed/old collections. p99 is fine. What have you established?
choices: Young-gen churn is happening; that is not automatically a pause incident
questions.explanation: Young GC is normal under allocation. An incident needs pause time, allocation rate, or old-gen growth — not ‘GC happened.’

questions.prompt: Native Memory Tracking summary shows Thread + Internal + GC far above the Java heap used. First question?
choices: How many threads, and what is the container/cgroup limit?
questions.explanation: Thread stacks and native grow with thread count. That is the container-OOM setup, not a reason to grow heap.

questions.prompt: A 512Mi cgroup and -Xmx512m on payment-service is wrong because:
choices: The JVM needs headroom for metaspace, stacks, code cache, and native; the cgroup kills the process when RSS exceeds 512Mi
questions.explanation: Heap = limit leaves no room for the rest of the process. Prefer MaxRAMPercentage < 100 or an explicit -Xmx below the cgroup.

questions.prompt: Spring Boot’s LaunchedURLClassLoader loads payment-service classes. What still belongs in metaspace?
choices: Class metadata for loaded classes and generated proxies
questions.explanation: Metaspace holds class metadata. Entity amounts are heap. Reloading class loaders without unloading is a metaspace-growth story.

questions.prompt: LAB-702 keeps a List of 200_000 payment records vs dropping them each iteration. What should differ?
choices: Nothing; the JIT erases all lists
Retained mode holds old-gen / used heap; transient mode shows allocation with objects becoming garbage
questions.explanation: Retention vs garbage is the point of the harness. Both allocate; only one keeps the objects live.
